title: Does a smaller batch with length-aware packing beat B1?
question: Consecutive original-order B4 lost to B1 by 1.46x. The generic batcher never sorts by length, so that protocol paid 36.73% padding overhead. Does a SMALLER batch with deterministic length-aware packing reach the 1.25x full-scorer adoption threshold?
_what_the_previous_pilot_did_not_establi: that padded model batching is unhelpful in general. It measured ONE protocol -- batch_size=4 AND original frozen order AND consecutive grouping AND right padding -- and four things varied at once.

protocols.role: separates the batch-size effect from the packing effect
did B4 fail because of its batch size or because of its packing?

_already_measured._not_rerun: it is measured; rerunning it would buy nothing

packing_policy.length_sorted_v1: sort by (token_length ascending, original_index ascending), split contiguously into groups of batch_size. No randomness, no device dependence, no model-family knowledge.
packing_policy._ascending: with a short final partial group, descending leaves the largest item paired with much shorter ones, which is the case that pads worst.
packing_policy._default_unchanged: micro_batches() still groups consecutively in the mixture's own order and still never sorts. Only this operator's step config selects a policy.

aggregation_order._rule: execution may reorder; aggregation may NOT.
aggregation_order._why: sorting changes batch composition. If it also changed the float summation order, a packing change would move two variables at once and neither could be attributed.
aggregation_order._how: the scorer writeseach value into per_item[layer][head][original_index]; the aggregation walks the frozen mixture from 0 to build subtype buckets.

identity._both_keys_are_hashed: calibration_forward_batch_size AND calibration_batch_packing. B2-consecutive and B2-sorted run the same number of forwards over the same items and can select different heads.

frozen_inputs._parent_reuse: search the durable store first; replay the 22-minute prefix at B1 only if the exact bytes are absent.

screen._why_these: early, middle and late depth. The model forward still traverses the whole model, so this measures kernel and packing throughput without paying for all 28 scorer layers.
screen._order_predeclared: frozen here before any timing is read. Whichever protocol runs first pays for allocator growth and autotuning the others do not.
screen._selection: the fastest non-reference candidate by measured wall time ALONE. No head-map or quality result selects which packing advances.

b1_comparability._meaning: if this session's P0 screen throughput agrees with the prior B1 evidence within +/-5%, the prior full B1 scorer may serve as the full-run reference. If it differs by more, a new full B1 must be run before any full-scorer speed claim.
b1_comparability._scaling: the prior full B1 scored 28 layers; the screen scores len(screen.layers). The prior is scaled by len(layers)/28 so the comparison is like with like.

full_scorer_gate.statistic: full-scorer reference seconds / candidate full-scorer seconds
full_scorer_gate._unchanged: the adoption threshold does NOT relax because this is a second optimization attempt.

decision_rules.then: STOP, no full scorer, no recovery

recovery_if_triggered._seed_state: PILOT-ONLY and NOT YET CONSUMED by recovery. Not a formal C3 seed; there is no formal C3 seed set.

structural_comparison.reference: the verified B1 causal landscape from the completed pilot

reuse_if_verifiable._else: generate a new B1 full scorer rather than approximating it

do_not_change: forward_kl_mean_batch chunk=512 -- a separate numerical variable
